sci-repo-y7-unk-bio-end-mc-1.title: Year 7 Science — Biology end-of-topic source test (original source MC)
sci-repo-y7-unk-bio-end-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all abiotic factors?
questions.explanation: B lists only nonliving factors. Soil contains living organisms, but soil as the physical substrate is an abiotic factor in this school model.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a resource a habitat needs to provide for an organism to survive?
questions.explanation: Money is not a biological habitat resource.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not an adaptation?
options: the position of the nostrils on a crocodile.
plants with hooks on their leaves to help them climb.
questions.explanation: A distribution statement (“kangaroos live in Australia”) is not itself a structural, physiological or behavioural adaptation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true?
options: a predator can never be a prey.
a prey can never be a predator.
a predator can also become a prey.
questions.explanation: A predator can itself be prey for another predator.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are introduced species in Australia?
questions.explanation: All listed species were introduced to Australia.

questions.prompt:
The fish shown below is adapted to its environment. Which characteristic will help it swim through the water?
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch13","id":"e11-image2"}]}]
options: the dark colour of its back and tail.
the long spines in its back fin.
questions.explanation: A streamlined shape reduces drag during swimming.

questions.prompt:
First-order consumers feed directly on producers. A producer can manufacture its own food. From the food web identify the group that are all first-order consumers.
Source context: questions 8, 9 and 10 all relate to the food web below:
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch13","id":"e11-image3"}]}]
questions.explanation: Sheep,insects,mallee fowl and rabbits all have a direct feeding connection from plants in the supplied web.

questions.prompt:
From the food web, identify which of the following is both a first and second order consumer.
Source context: questions 8, 9 and 10 all relate to the food web below:
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch13","id":"e11-image3"}]}]
questions.explanation: Mallee fowl feed directly on plants and on insects, occupying first/second consumer roles.

sci-repo-y7-unk-chem-mid-mc-1.title: Year 7 Science — Chemistry and investigating mid-topic source test (original source MC)
sci-repo-y7-unk-chem-mid-mc-1.parent: Chemistry and investigating mid-topic source test
sci-repo-y7-unk-chem-mid-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all correct?
options: Chemistry – Science of materials, Geology – Science of rocks, Psychology- Science of forces.
Ecology – Science of the environment, Astronomy – Science of the universe, Chemistry – Science of materials.
Biology – Science of living things, Ecology – Science of plants and animals, Geology – Science of rocks.
Physics – Science of forces, Astronomy – Science of asteroids, Ecology – Science of the environment.
questions.explanation: B is the most accurate set:ecology studies relationships involving organisms/environment,astronomy celestial objects/universe,chemistry matter and change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lists contains only measuring equipment?
options: a beaker, a graduated cylinder, a conical flask and an electronic scale.
a measuring cylinder, a test-tube, a conical flask and a spatula.
a beaker, a graduated cylinder, a test-tube and a filter funnel.
a measuring cylinder, a evaporating basin, a beaker and a conical flask.
questions.explanation: A is intended:beaker/cylinder/flask can estimate volumes and scales measure mass;beakers/flasks are much less precise than volumetric apparatus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a safety rule in a Science laboratory?
options: always wear safety glasses when using chemicals.
do not eat, taste, drink or sniff anything unless told to by a teacher.
if you break something immediately get rid of it.
questions.explanation: D. Report breakage immediately and follow safe cleanup instructions;do not simply dispose of broken equipment yourself. Never taste or directly sniff laboratory materials.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a mixture?
questions.explanation: D. Air,seawater and paint are mixtures.

questions.prompt: A solvent is:
options: a substance that does not dissolve.
the substance that dissolves the other one.
when a substance dissolves in another, forming a clear mixture.
questions.explanation: C. Solvent is the component in which a solute dissolves.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all ways to separate an insoluble substance from a liquid?
options: decantation, filtration, sieving and gravity separation.
distillation , decantation, filtration and gravity separation.
gravity separation, evaporation, filtration and chromatography.
questions.explanation: A. Decantation,filtration,sieving/straining at suitable particle size and gravity settling can separate insoluble material.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is soluble in water?
questions.explanation: B. Common salt dissolves in water under ordinary conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an inference?
options: it must be nearly home time.
questions.explanation: B is an inference from evidence;C is a prediction andA/D are observations.

questions.prompt: Which of the abbreviations for the units are all correct?
options: gram – g, litre – L, kilogram – kg, millimetre – mm, minutes – min.
gram – gm, litre – L, kilogram – kg, millimetre – mm, minutes – min.
gram – g, litre – l, kilogram – kg, millimetre – ml, minutes – min.
gram – g, litre – L, kilogram – kgm, millimetre – mm, minutes – mins.
questions.explanation: A. g,L,kg,mm,min are correct unit symbols.

questions.prompt: Which graph would you use for a set of continuous data, such as time and temperature?
questions.explanation: C. A line graph can show how continuous temperature varies with time.

sci-repo-y7-unk-phys-end-mc-1.title: Year 7 Science — Forces and simple machines source test (original source MC)
sci-repo-y7-unk-phys-end-mc-1.parent: Forces and simple machines source test
sci-repo-y7-unk-phys-end-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: A force can change:
options: the speed something is moving at.
questions.explanation: Forces can change direction,speed and shape.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct:
options: the more massive something is, the greater its inertia.
the less massive something is, the greater its inertia.
the more massive something is, the less its inertia.
the mass of something has no effect on inertia.
questions.explanation: Greater mass means greater inertia.

questions.prompt: Active safety features are designed to reduce the chance of an accident happening. Passive safety features lessen the possible damage to the occupants when an accident does happen. Which of the following are all active safety features?
options: electronic stability control, good tyres, reversing sensors.
questions.explanation: B. Stability control,tyres and reversing sensors help prevent a crash.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all methods to reduce friction?
options: polishing, increase surface area, rough surfaces.
questions.explanation: C. Lubrication,air layers and streamlining can reduce relevant friction/drag.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about gravity is true?
options: gravity pushes objects towards the Earth.
all objects naturally attract each other.
questions.explanation: C. Masses exert gravitational attraction;gravity is noncontact.

questions.prompt: Atoms are made up of the following subatomic particles:
questions.explanation: A. Protons,electrons and usually neutrons make up atoms;hydrogen-1 has no neutron.

questions.prompt: Static electricity occurs when:
options: insulators move from one charged object to another.
neutrons move from one charged object to another.
protons move from one charged object to another.
electrons move from one charged object to another.
questions.explanation: D. In ordinary charging by contact/rubbing,electrons transfer and leave charge imbalance.

questions.prompt: A wheelbarrow is an example of a:
questions.explanation: B. Load lies between fulcrum and effort in a wheelbarrow(second-class lever).

sci-repo-y8-unk-earth-end-mc-1.title: Year 8 Science — Rocks,minerals and investigating source test (original source MC)
sci-repo-y8-unk-earth-end-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a type of sedimentary rock?
questions.explanation: Plastic is not a conventional sedimentary-rock category;clastic,chemical and organic are.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is not true about sedimentary rocks?
questions.explanation: A is false:cooling magma produces igneous rock.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all sedimentary rocks?
options: sandstone, limestone, mudstone, conglomerate and basalt.
sandstone, limestone, mudstone, conglomerate and breccia.
limestone, breccia, conglomerate, granite and siltstone.
granite, pumice, conglomerate, basalt and gneiss.
questions.explanation: B:sandstone,limestone,mudstone,conglomerate,breccia are sedimentary.

questions.prompt: The formation of sedimentary rocks in the rock cycle involves:
options: weathering and erosion of other rocks first.
questions.explanation: A is intended for clastic sedimentary rocks.Not all sedimentary rocks require prior rock-fragment erosion;chemical/biogenic formation also occurs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not true about metamorphic rocks?
options: they form from heat and/or pressure.
they can contain precious gems such as sapphires.
gneiss, marble, slate and schist are all examples of metamorphic rock.
questions.explanation: C is false:metamorphic rocks commonly contain crystals.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not correct in the formation of metamorphic rocks?
questions.explanation: D is wrong:basalt is igneous,not the metamorphic product of conglomerate.

questions.prompt: The dependent variable is:
options: the variable you measure or observe.
the variable you keep the same.
questions.explanation: Dependent variable is measured/observed.

questions.prompt: Which piece of equipment would be used to measure exactly 27ml of a liquid?
questions.explanation: Measuring cylinder is best among the listed choices,but no physical measurement is literally exact;resolution matters.

questions.prompt: The main physical properties used to identify minerals are:
questions.explanation: Hardness,lustre,colour and streak are useful physical identification properties.
